messages:
Eli: FYI onboarding request for 'psimodel-v2' from external repo. License looks mixed — repo has CC-BY-4.0 but also a PATENT_LICENSE.md that talks about 'commercial restrictions'. Need legal take for Hosted/Dedicated + whether we can ship quantized weights. Link: https://git.example.com/psimodel-v2 :eyes:
Maria (Legal): quick skim — top-level LICENSE = CC-BY-4.0, but PATENT_LICENSE.md contains a research-use-only patent reservation. That could block commercial hosting. I need the exact wording; can you paste the snippet? cc @Alex (PM)
Ash: If that patent clause restricts commercial deployment, we can't offer it on Hosted or sell it via Dedicated. Also unclear if quantized weights count as redistribution/derivative. Can you paste?
Eli: Sure — snippet from PATENT_LICENSE.md:
```
PATENT_LICENSE
This model and associated weights are provided for research purposes only. Any commercial deployment, redistribution, or exploitation requires an explicit patent license from the contributors. Quantized or converted weight files are considered derivatives and subject to the same restriction.
```
Maria (Legal): that's pretty explicit. "Research purposes only" will preclude commercial hosting. Action items: 1) ask upstream for an explicit commercial + redistribution + derivative license (a short addendum), 2) if they refuse, we can't host or ship quantized binaries. Internal evals might be ok but need confirmation. I'll draft an email.
Alex (PM): For Dedicated customers we typically ship container images with weights — that would be redistribution. For Private deployments where customer brings their own infra, it's less clear but if we package weights it's still redistribution. Can legal confirm?
Sam (Infra): confirmed — shipping a container with weights == redistribution. Even providing an image in a marketplace is redistribution. "Bring-your-own" (BYO weights) could be a workaround but reduces product experience.
Ash: technical note — quantization tool we use emits .q4_0 and we usually sign the blob. If derivatives are disallowed, this counts as creating a derivative. So we need explicit permission to export quantized files.
Maria (Legal): good point. CC-BY-4.0 alone allows derivatives with attribution but the separate PATENT_LICENSE overrides for patent rights. So we have a conflict: copyright license permits derivation but patent reservation restricts commercial exploitation/derivative distribution. Steps: (a) ask upstream for explicit commercial use + derivative redistribution permission, (b) if denied, allow only internal non-customer evals under a signed MOU, (c) block Hosted and quantized export in onboarding until resolved.
Eli: Can we do an internal staging eval (no external users, no billing) while we wait? That would help perf/quality checks.
Maria (Legal): internal eval is lower risk but not zero. I'll prepare a quick intake form to capture: will weights be redistributed, will we bill end users, will quantized weights be exported, will training data include NC/ND datasets, etc. Complete that and we can assess under "internal evaluation" exception.
Ash: I'll fill the form. Also propose a gating flag in model onboarding UI: if patent-encumbered -> block hosted enroll & quant export until approved.
Sam (Infra): +1. Also flagging dataset provenance: I spotted DATAPROVENANCE.md referencing some CC-BY-NC image sets. If training data includes NC (non-commercial) items that could cascade into model restrictions depending on jurisdiction. Can legal check dataset licenses too?
Eli: ran a quick grep, DATAPROVENANCE.md lists a few CC-BY-NC sources and an unlabeled scrape of public forums. Not great. Pasting file path: /repo/DATAPROVENANCE.md
Maria (Legal): NC in the upstream dataset can indeed create a downstream noncommercial obligation in some cases. We need the upstream to provide provenance docs and confirmation they had rights to relicense model for commercial use. I'll include dataset provenance and patent license in the outreach.
Alex (PM): timeline — two customers asked about preloaded Dedicated images next week. Can we get a legal decision by EOD Wed?
Maria (Legal): I'll prioritize. Drafting outreach to upstream now and will add a short MOU template for internal evals. Putting temporary hold on Hosted onboarding and quant exports until we get explicit permission or a replacement model.
DeployBot: label applied: legal-review-pending :warning:
Eli: thanks — ping back here when you have the draft email and the intake form link.
Maria (Legal): will do.
